implementation_notes: In .NET the substitute is a library artifact: a Polly ResiliencePipelineBuilder<T> declares the fallback with FallbackStrategyOptions<T> (ShouldHandle selects the outcomes, FallbackAction produces the substitute, OnFallback records it) and ExecuteAsync runs the call through the retry, breaker and fallback chain; Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience wires the same pipeline to HttpClient, so per-dependency degradation is configuration rather than an if-tree. That pipeline is what replaces the hand-written degraded-mode controller; write that controller by hand only when the degraded answer must be assembled from several dependencies or domain rules the pipeline cannot see. ASP.NET Core contributes the surrounding behaviour (health checks and a cached/read-only path for the UI).
pitfalls: FallbackAction runs on the failure path: keep it allocation-light and non-throwing - throwing from a Polly delegate disrupts the pipeline and is documented as an anti-pattern.
ShouldHandle defaults to any exception except OperationCanceledException, so an unconfigured fallback also degrades on programming errors; narrow it to the dependency's exception types.
A fallback that returns null or blank DTOs is indistinguishable downstream: put the degraded state in the response (a flag or header), not only in telemetry.
